derivation.function: fn=lambda d: d / 2 - PAD_HALF_F,

brakes.bias_front_hydraulic.description: Front share of brake torque at equal line pressure (no EBD)

candidates.how_to_measure: Measure piston diameters and pad heights; or log front/rear line pressure.
candidates.notes: Not computable: missing inputs ['brakes.front_piston_diameter', 'brakes.rear_piston_diameter']. Equal pad mu front/rear assumed; real bias also set by EBD. Torque share, not force at the tire.

derivation.function: fn=lambda df, dr, rf, rr: _share(df, dr, rf, rr, PAD_HALF_F, PAD_HALF_R),

candidates.how_to_measure: Head-on long-lens photo with a scale; integrate the silhouette (incl. mirrors and tires) by script.

engine.displacement_from_bore_stroke.description: Swept volume computed from bore, stroke and 4 cylinders (cross-check of published 1498 cc)

candidates.how_to_measure: n/a (geometry)
candidates.notes: Range from +/-0.05 mm print rounding. Should match engine.displacement (1.498e-3 m3) within ~0.1%.

derivation.function: fn=lambda bore, stroke: 4 * math.pi / 4 * bore ** 2 * stroke,

mass.fuel_mass_full.description: Fuel mass with a full tank

candidates.how_to_measure: Weigh the car with a full and a near-empty tank.
candidates.notes: m_fuel = V * rho; range from specific gravity 0.71-0.77.

derivation.function: fn=lambda vol, rho: vol * rho,

candidates.how_to_measure: Axle or corner scales, full tank, no driver.
candidates.notes: m_f = m * f_front; range +/-0.5 pp on the published distribution.

derivation.function: fn=lambda m, ff: m * ff,

candidates.how_to_measure: Axle or corner scales, full tank, no driver.
candidates.notes: m_r = m * (1 - f_front).

derivation.function: fn=lambda m, ff: m * (1 - ff),

mass.cg_y.description: Longitudinal CG position (vehicle Y; front axle = 0, rear axle = -wheelbase)

candidates.how_to_measure: Axle scales: distance behind front axle = L * m_rear / m.
candidates.notes: Static moment balance: a = L * (1 - f_front) behind the front axle.

derivation.function: fn=lambda L, ff: -(1 - ff) * L,

mass.cg_height.description: CG height above ground at curb (from NHTSA SSF)

candidates.how_to_measure: Axle-lift method: weigh the rear axle with the front raised by >= 0.5 m (wheels on scales, suspension locked); h = r + L*dW/(W*tan(theta)). Or use a tilt table.
candidates.notes: h = T_avg / (2 SSF), with this car's tracks and NHTSA's measured SSF 1.48 (printed to 0.01). The SSF test vehicle is probably a 2022 Civic Sedan, so +/-15 mm is added for body/wheel/load differences (assumption). Cross-check: the published NHTSA rollover possibility reproduces from SSF 1.48 (mass.check_rollover_risk_from_ssf).

derivation.function: fn=lambda tf, tr, ssf: _tavg(tf, tr) / (2 * ssf),

mass.check_rollover_risk_from_ssf.description: Cross-check: NHTSA no-tip-up risk model evaluated at the SSF (compare with mass.rollover_possibility_nhtsa = 0.095)

candidates.how_to_measure: n/a (consistency check of government data).
candidates.notes: 68 FR 59291 no-tip-up model. Agreement with 0.095 confirms the SSF row and the model are consistent.

derivation.function: fn=lambda ssf: 1.0 / (1.0 + math.exp(2.8891 + 1.1686 * math.log(ssf - 0.90))),

mass.inertia_yaw.description: Yaw moment of inertia about the CG (whole car, curb)

candidates.how_to_measure: Yaw inertia rig (bifilar/trifilar pendulum or NHTSA IPMD-type facility); not practical at home.
candidates.notes: Izz = m (c_z L)^2, c_z = mean of sqrt(Jzz/m)/L over the VIPD 'Passenger Small' and 'Passenger Large' class means (about 0.54). The VIPD table lists sprung mass; applying the ratio to curb mass is an assumption covered by the range.

derivation.function: fn=lambda m, L: _inertia(m, L, "yaw"),

mass.inertia_pitch.description: Pitch moment of inertia about the CG (whole car, curb)

candidates.how_to_measure: Pitch inertia pendulum test (specialist facility).
candidates.notes: Iyy(pitch) = m (c_p L)^2 with c_p from VIPD class means (about 0.52).

derivation.function: fn=lambda m, L: _inertia(m, L, "pitch"),

mass.inertia_roll.description: Roll moment of inertia about the CG (whole car, curb)

candidates.how_to_measure: Roll inertia pendulum test (specialist facility).
candidates.notes: Ixx(roll) = m (c_r T_avg)^2 with c_r = sqrt(Jxx/m)/T from VIPD class means (about 0.45).

derivation.function: fn=lambda m, tf, tr: _inertia(m, _tavg(tf, tr), "roll"),

candidates.how_to_measure: n/a (consistency check).
candidates.notes: Range shown is the published VIPD band; the value should fall inside it.

derivation.function: fn=lambda iz, ix: iz / ix,

candidates.notes: Arithmetic closure check.

steering.max_angle_outer.description: Outer front road-wheel angle at full lock, from the curb-to-curb turning circle

candidates.how_to_measure: Turn plates at full lock left and right (alignment rig turning-angle readout); +/-0.5 deg.
candidates.notes: delta_o = asin(L / (D/2 - h)), h = contact-patch half width (0.105 m, range 0.090-0.1175). Turn centre on rear-axle line.

derivation.function: fn=lambda D, L: _outer(D, L, HALF_TREAD),

steering.max_angle_inner.description: Inner front road-wheel angle at full lock assuming 100 % Ackermann (pure geometry from the turning circle)

candidates.how_to_measure: Turn plates at full lock; read the inner wheel angle directly.
candidates.notes: delta_i = atan(L / (sqrt((D/2-h)^2 - L^2) - track_f)). Assumes 100 % Ackermann, which the published turning circle cannot verify; compare steering.ackermann_pct_estimate.

derivation.function: fn=lambda D, L, tf: _inner_ackermann(D, L, tf, HALF_TREAD),

steering.mean_lock_angle_from_ratio.description: Mean front road-wheel angle at lock implied by turns lock-to-lock and published ratio

candidates.how_to_measure: Turn plates at full lock (average of inner and outer).
candidates.notes: theta = turns*360/2/ratio. Valid only if Honda's ratio is the overall (lock) ratio; range covers rounding of the printed figures only.

derivation.function:
def _mean_lock_from_ratio(turns, ratio):
    return math.radians(turns * 360.0 / 2.0 / ratio)

steering.crosscheck_ratio_vs_turning_cir.description: Cross-check: mean lock angle from ratio / mean lock angle from turning circle at 100 % Ackermann (1.00 = consistent)

candidates.how_to_measure: Turn plates at full lock.
candidates.notes: Values within ~0.9-1.1 support reading Honda's ratio as an overall ratio; a value well above 1 would mean the printed ratio is slower than the true lock-average (e.g. an on-centre ratio).

derivation.function:
fn=lambda D, L, tf, turns, ratio: _mean_lock_from_ratio(turns, ratio) / (
            0.5 * (_outer(D, L, HALF_TREAD) + _inner_ackermann(D, L, tf, HALF_TREAD))),

steering.ackermann_pct_estimate.description: Ackermann percentage estimate: (inner_actual - outer) / (inner_100% - outer), inner_actual = 2*mean_lock(ratio) - outer

candidates.how_to_measure: Turn plates: inner and outer angles at full lock and at 20 deg outer (toe-out-on-turns spec on an alignment printout).
candidates.notes: Fraction (1.0 = 100 % Ackermann). Very sensitive: it rests on the published ratio being the exact lock-average and on the contact-patch assumption. Range is widened to include 0.6-1.0, the usual road-car band, because the inputs cannot rule it out.

derivation.function: fn=lambda D, L, tf, turns, ratio: _ackermann_pct(D, L, tf, turns, ratio, HALF_TREAD) / 100.0,

tires.sidewall_height_nominal.description: Nominal sidewall height (width x aspect ratio)

candidates.how_to_measure: Measure tire OD and rim flange diameter; (OD - rim)/2.
candidates.notes: Exact arithmetic on the size code; real tires vary about +/-2 %.

derivation.function: fn=lambda w, ar: sidewall(w, ar),

tires.overall_diameter_nominal.description: Nominal unloaded overall diameter from the size code

candidates.how_to_measure: Tape the circumference of an inflated, unloaded tire (/pi), +/-1 mm.
candidates.notes: OD = rim + 2 x width x aspect ratio. 235/40R18 -> 0.6452 m.

derivation.function: fn=lambda w, ar, rim: od_nominal(w, ar, rim),

tires.rolling_circumference.description: Rolling circumference (distance per wheel revolution), estimated from nominal size

candidates.how_to_measure: Mark the tread and floor, roll the loaded car 5-10 revolutions in a straight line, divide distance by revolutions (+/-0.3 %); or use the OE tire maker's revs/km.
candidates.notes: C_roll = pi x OD_nominal x 0.97 (range 0.96-0.985); the factor is an engineering assumption, not a cited figure. Superseded by maker revs/km once the OE tire is known.

derivation.function: fn=lambda w, ar, rim: math.pi * od_nominal(w, ar, rim) * ROLL_FACTOR,

tires.loaded_radius.description: Static loaded radius (axle to ground), estimated

candidates.how_to_measure: With the car at curb weight and placard pressure, measure hub-centre height above the floor at each corner (+/-1 mm).
candidates.notes: r_loaded = OD_nominal/2 - deflection; deflection 18 mm (range 12-25 mm) is a judgment for a 40-series tire at placard pressure.

derivation.function: fn=lambda w, ar, rim: od_nominal(w, ar, rim) / 2 - DEFL,

drivetrain.pred_rpm_at_100kmh_6th.description: Predicted engine speed at 100 km/h in 6th (no slip), for comparison with observed tach readings

candidates.how_to_measure: Hold a GPS-verified 100 km/h in 6th on level road and log engine rpm via OBD-II (PID 0x0C).
candidates.notes: rpm = v * g6 * FD * 60 / C_roll. Range = +/-1.5 % rolling circumference. Compare with drivetrain.obs_* records.

derivation.function: fn=(lambda g6, fd, circ, _s=_spd: rpm_at_speed(_s, g6, fd, circ)),

drivetrain.pred_rpm_at_70mph_6th.description: Predicted engine speed at 70 mph in 6th (no slip), for comparison with observed tach readings

candidates.how_to_measure: Hold a GPS-verified 70 mph in 6th on level road and log engine rpm via OBD-II (PID 0x0C).
candidates.notes: rpm = v * g6 * FD * 60 / C_roll. Range = +/-1.5 % rolling circumference. Compare with drivetrain.obs_* records.

derivation.function: fn=(lambda g6, fd, circ, _s=_spd: rpm_at_speed(_s, g6, fd, circ)),

tables.description: Speed per 1000 rpm and at redline/limiter per gear, from resolved ratios and tyre rolling circumference (no slip). Reverse row included. Ratios are never tuned to match observations.

Stock dyno points from engine_curves/ runs flagged use_for_curve (wheel measured, crank = wheel/(1-loss)). As of Phase 1 no stock 6MT hatch run with rpm-resolved points was found, so the table has no rows.
